newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices mixed, influenced by weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices mixed, influenced by weather.

text.p: Influenced by differing weather patterns, U.S. spot natgas prices were mixed Friday but were still hanging above index levels, industry sources said.

Gulf Coast prices edged a few cents over index levels into the mid-to-high $2.70s. The higher-priced deals were evident in late trading as weekend temperatures in the Northeast were expected to dip to levels about 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
At the Henry Hub, La., traders reported closing deals as high as $2.80 shortly before the nomination deadlines.
In the Midwest, however, swing prices eased into the mid-$2.60s, down more than five cents from Thursday's discussion but still about 10 cents over November indices.

Sources attributed the softening to milder temperatures expected this weekend in the region. The respite from the cold is expected to be brief though in the central northern plains as forecasters are calling for below-normal temperatures again next week.

In west Texas, the normal drop in weekend demand and moderating temperatures pushed Permian prices into the low-to-mid $2.60s, down about five cents from Thursday but still more than 10 cents over November index levels.
Weekend prices at the southern California border softened into the high-$2.70s to low-$2.80s.

Defying the cooling trend in the East, New York city-gate prices fell into the low-$3 area in late trading. Earlier deals were reported done in the $3.20s and $3.30s. The cold spell in the Northeast should be short-lived as a warming trend is anticipated by mid-week.
Similarly in the Appalachian region, late prices slumped into the high-$2.80s, down more than 20 cents from index levels.
